value.body: A calibration engineer checks measuring instruments — gauges, meters, sensors, weighing and test equipment — against reference standards and issues calibration records. Employers include calibration laboratories, manufacturing plants, pharma companies and instrument service firms. A typical day involves running calibrations, working out measurement uncertainty, and keeping equipment and documents ready for audits.

items.label: Typical entry
items.value: B.Tech Instrumentation, Electronics or Electrical; diploma holders also enter

items.label: Work setting
items.value: Calibration labs and on site at client plants

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Freshers usually join a NABL-accredited calibration lab or a plant's quality or metrology team as a trainee. A short course in metrology or ISO/IEC 17025 and comfort with documentation help.

value.title: At a glance
items: Work is precise and procedure-driven, and audits are a regular part of the job.
On-site calibration involves travel to client plants.
Next roles: senior calibration engineer, lab technical manager, quality manager.
